header.running_head: Condemning Rulers who Live Lives Above the Standards of the Common People and who Veil Themselves from people in Need

blocks.text: instructed him to fetch water from the well to give the camels to drink. The man continued going in and out of the well until he was exhausted. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then asked him, "How much longer will you be in this world?" "For only a short while," came the reply. Hadhrat Umar (RA) commented, "Then is it for this short while that you have built the mansion and adopted a standard of living that exceeds those of the poor, the widows and orphans? Go back to your post and never repeat yourself." [^1]
Hadhrat Umar (RA) Takes Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) to task for Building a Mansion

Hadhrat Attaab bin Rifaa'ah narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once received the news that Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) had built a mansion and had a door put on it, saying that the noise from the marketplace has now been cut off (form entering the mansion). Hadhrat Umar (RA) then dispatched Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslama (RA), whom he always sent when he needed a task done exactly as he wanted. The instructions he gave Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslama (RA) was to bring Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) to him and to burn down the door.
(When Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslama (RA) arrived in Kufa) Someone came to Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) and informed him (about the arrival) and when the features (of Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslama (RA)) were described to Hadhrat Sa'd (RA), he recognised him. Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) then went to meet Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslama (RA), who said to him, "The news has reached the Ameerul Mu'mineen that you commented about the noise being cut off." When Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) swore that he never made such a statement, Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslama (RA) said, "We shall do as we have been commanded while you will have to convey what you said (to the Ameerul Mu'mineen)."
When Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) offered to provide Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslama (RA) with provisions for the journey, he refused to take any and rode off until he reached Madinah. When Hadhrat Umar (RA) saw him, he said, "If I did not have a good opinion of you, I would have thought that you did not fulfil the task." Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslama (RA) informed Hadhrat Umar (RA) that he had hurried back and assured Hadhrat Umar (RA), "I have fulfilled the task. However, Sa'd (RA) excuses himself and swears that he had never made the statement."
Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked, "Did he give you any provisions for the journey?" Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslama (RA) replied, "No, but what prevented you from giving me provisions?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "I disliked giving you any provisions because although you would have had ease, I would have had to suffer for it (in the Aakhirah) since hunger is killing the people around me in Madinah. Have you not heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say that a Mu'min should not fill his belly while his neighbour goes hungry?"[^2]
Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.3 Pg.166).
